craft_claim: Humour requires a simultaneous violation and a benign framing; if the violation is not made benign for the audience, amusement collapses into offence or discomfort.

supporting_evidence.note: Moral violations judged simultaneously benign elicit amusement; three routes to benign-ness are identified: an alternative norm, a large psychological distance, and a weak commitment to the violated norm.

counterevidence.note: The dossier records superiority, relief and incongruity as rival partial families of humour theory and warns against presenting one as the whole explanation (dossier sections B and C); the simultaneous-benign requirement is a feature of the benign-violation account rather than an established general condition of humour.

scope: Humour involving norms, moral content, and social taboos, across forms.
exceptions: Audiences that reject the benign framing read the same content as offensive rather than funny.
The benign route is audience-relative; a framing that works for one group can fail for another.
